difficultyAxis: Entity count and referential depth: seven entities wired by explicit foreign keys, so every stage must iterate the whole graph instead of handling the first entity.
rationale: A logistics service whose entities reference each other by identifier: Shipment points at Warehouse, Carrier and Address; ShipmentItem, RouteLeg and TrackingEvent all point back at Shipment; RouteLeg points at two Addresses. A stage that resolves only one entity, or that assumes every entity is independent, produces a partial service here while the two-entity fixtures still pass.

userStories.intent: register a warehouse with its region and capacity
userStories.benefit: shipments can be routed from a known facility

scenarios.given: a unique warehouse code and a positive capacity
scenarios.when: the operator registers the warehouse
scenarios.then: the warehouse is persisted and returned with its generated identifier

scenarios.given: a capacity of zero or less
scenarios.when: the operator attempts to register the warehouse
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid before reaching the service layer

scenarios.given: no warehouse exists with the requested identifier
scenarios.when: the operator retrieves that warehouse
scenarios.then: the service reports the resource as not found

userStories.intent: register a carrier with a service level and a contact address
userStories.benefit: shipments are assigned to a compliant transport provider

scenarios.given: a carrier code matching the permitted pattern and a service level
scenarios.when: the planner registers the carrier
scenarios.then: the carrier is persisted and returned with its generated identifier

scenarios.given: a carrier code that does not match the permitted pattern
scenarios.when: the planner attempts to register the carrier
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid before reaching the service layer

userStories.intent: record a destination address with a postal code and country
userStories.benefit: deliveries can be geocoded and routed

scenarios.given: a complete address with a well-formed postal code
scenarios.when: the planner records the address
scenarios.then: the address is persisted and returned with its generated identifier

scenarios.given: a latitude outside the permitted range
scenarios.when: the planner attempts to record the address
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: dispatch a shipment from a warehouse through a carrier to an address
userStories.benefit: goods leave the facility under a tracked reference

scenarios.given: an existing warehouse, an existing carrier, an existing destination address and a positive total weight
scenarios.when: the dispatcher creates the shipment
scenarios.then: the shipment is persisted with its warehouse, carrier and destination references intact

scenarios.given: a shipment referencing a carrier identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the dispatcher attempts to create the shipment
scenarios.then: the service rejects the shipment and reports the missing carrier reference

scenarios.given: a total weight below the permitted minimum
scenarios.when: the dispatcher attempts to create the shipment
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid before reaching the service layer

userStories.intent: add packing items to a dispatched shipment
userStories.benefit: the shipment contents and declared value are auditable

scenarios.given: an existing shipment and an item quantity within the permitted range
scenarios.when: the dispatcher adds the item
scenarios.then: the item is persisted against the shipment and returned with its identifier

scenarios.given: an item quantity above the permitted maximum
scenarios.when: the dispatcher attempts to add the item
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

scenarios.given: a shipment identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the dispatcher attempts to add an item to it
scenarios.then: the service reports the shipment as not found

userStories.intent: plan the ordered legs of a shipment route
userStories.benefit: each leg can be tracked and measured independently

scenarios.given: an existing shipment, two existing addresses and an arrival later than the departure
scenarios.when: the planner records the leg
scenarios.then: the leg is persisted with its sequence number and both address references

scenarios.given: a planned arrival earlier than the planned departure
scenarios.when: the planner attempts to record the leg
scenarios.then: the service rejects the leg as inconsistent

scenarios.given: a sequence number below the permitted minimum
scenarios.when: the planner attempts to record the leg
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: record tracking events against a shipment in occurrence order
userStories.benefit: the customer-facing timeline reflects what actually happened

scenarios.given: an existing shipment and an occurrence time in the past
scenarios.when: the operator records the tracking event
scenarios.then: the event is persisted against the shipment with its occurrence time

scenarios.given: an occurrence time in the future
scenarios.when: the operator attempts to record the event
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: read the shipments dispatched from a warehouse

scenarios.given: a warehouse with no dispatched shipments
scenarios.when: the planner reads the shipments for that warehouse
scenarios.then: the service returns an empty collection rather than reporting an error

scenarios.given: a warehouse identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the planner reads the shipments for that warehouse
scenarios.then: the service reports the warehouse as not found
